newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH outperforms bourse ahead of meeting.
newsitem.headline: LVMH outperforms bourse ahead of meeting.

text.p: Shares in LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton outperformed the bourse on Wednesday and briefly hit a year high on expectations that chairman Bernard Arnault's view would prevail at a meeting today with the chairmen of merger partners Guinness and Grand Metropolitan.
"Investors are betting on the establishment of a drinks group in which LVMH would have the biggest stake," one analyst said.
Shares in LVMH were down 1.13 percent at 1,581 francs at 1040 GMT, weighed down by a sudden downturn in the market. The CAC-40 index was 2.2 percent lower.

Earlier the stock hit a new year high of 1,642 francs, a gain of around six percent since the news broke that the three chairmen would meet to air their differences over the proposed Guinness-Grand Met merger.
Arnault, Guinness's Tony Greener and George Bull of Grand Met will meet at LVMH headquarters today at 1200 GMT.

Arnault, the largest single shareholder in Guinness and Grand Met through LVMH's respective stakes of 14.2 percent and 6.4 percent, will reiterate his standing proposal -- a merger of the three companies' drinks businesses in a group to be listed.

The stock had sunk last month to a low of 1,461 francs on investor nervousness after LVMH began buying up shares in Grand Met in an apparent bid to line up a large enough holding to block the merger. It has spent more than eight billion francs ($1.4 billion) to buy 6.4 percent of Grand Met.

Arnault previously put pressure on the British companies by launching legal action to defend his right to exercise options to buy Guinness out of their valuable joint distribution ventures if it went ahead and merged with Grand Met.

Analysts say Arnault is in a strong bargaining position. His threat to take his proposal to Grand Met's shareholders looks credible, and his argument that it makes more sense industrially to create a drinks company is attractive.
They estimate a three-way drinks company would boost LVMH's results. "Not by a lot in the short term, but it would be interesting in the longer term," one analyst said.
"At first glance, it's profit-enhancing because Arnault would get 30 percent of a much more profitable group than the company formed by a merger of Guinness and Grand Met," another analyst said.
"I have a strong feeling that Guinness is ready to negotiate," the analyst added.
The Daily Telegraph recently reported that a three-way drinks merger could generate up to 85 million pounds ($141.5 million) in additional savings.

British newspapers have said Guinness and Grand Met may propose to include Moet Hennessy -- LVMH's drinks subsidiary in which Guinness holds 34 percent -- in UDV, the new company formed by the merger of the Guinness United Distillers and Grand Met IDV drinks businesses.
In turn, LVMH would take a stake in UDV, and analysts estimate the holding would be 30 to 35 percent.
They say other issues to be sorted out the valuation of Moet Hennessy and Arnault's role in the new ensemble.
